title: Nuclear DNA purification from recalcitrant plant species for long-read sequencing
author: Ashley Jones

steps.title: Homogenize Plant Tissue
steps.instruction: Process plant leaves to create a homogenate for nuclei isolation.

substeps.instruction: Place 50 g of leaves into a blender with enough nuclei isolation buffer to cover the blades (approximately 150 mL).
Homogenize the tissue on max speed.
Transfer the homogenate to a beaker, repeatedly washing out the blender with nuclei isolation buffer (500 mL buffer allocated per extraction).
Clean the blender with tap water, 70% ethanol, and then MQW before processing subsequent samples.

steps.title: Filter Homogenate
steps.instruction: Perform sequential filtration to isolate nuclei and remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Filter homogenate using a sieve (or disk membrane mesh placed in a funnel) into a 1 L Schott bottle, forcibly squeezing out residual homogenate.
Filter the resulting homogenate through 1 layer of Miracloth using a funnel and 1 L Schott bottle, gently squeezing the residue.
Repeat filtration through 2 layers of Miracloth, then 4 layers, using new Schott bottles.
Perform a final gravity filtration through 8 layers of Miracloth (no squeezing) into a 500 mL Nalgene bottle.

steps.title: Isolate and Wash Nuclei
steps.instruction: Purify the nuclei pellet through a series of centrifugation and wash steps.

substeps.instruction: Add 2.5 mL of 100% Triton X-100, or 25 mL of 10% Triton X-100 (final concentration 0.5%).
Incubate the mixture on an ice bath with gentle rocking for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 600 rcf and 4°C for 20 minutes.
Weigh Nalgene bottles with contents and lids to ensure balance and verify the o-ring is intact.
Centrifuge at 600 rcf and 4°C for 30 minutes (e.g., 4,600 rpm on a Sorvall RC5C using rotor SLA-3000 (00)).
Discard the supernatant and add up to 450 mL of nuclei wash buffer per Nalgene bottle (save 100 mL).
Gently resuspend the pellet using a large fine hair paint brush soaked in freshly made pre-chilled nuclei wash buffer.
Discard supernatant and repeat the wash with another ~450 mL of nuclei wash buffer until the pellet is grey-white with no traces of green.
After the final spin down, discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet with 50 mL of nuclei wash buffer; transfer evenly across two 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Repeat the resuspension with another 50 mL of buffer and add to the two Falcon tubes.
Centrifuge at 600 rcf and 4°C for 30 minutes.
Optional: Transfer supernatant into new 50 mL Falcon tubes and centrifuge at 1,000 rcf and 4°C for 30 minutes to recover a small pellet.

steps.title: Lyse Nuclei
steps.instruction: Break open the nuclei to release the genomic DNA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10 mL of fresh lysis buffer per sample, ideally pre-heated at 50-65°C (solution must be clear).
Add 10 mL of lysis buffer to a 3-5 mL nuclei pellet (usually one of the two Falcon tubes from the previous step) and vortex vigorously for 1 min (final SDS concentration ~2%).
Add RNAse A and Proteinase K to the solution (recommended concentration 50-100 µg/mL each) and mix by swirling and inverting.
Incubate the samples at 50-60°C for 1 h, shaking at 400-900 rpm if possible.

steps.title: Precipitate Proteins and Polysaccharides
steps.instruction: Remove contaminants using potassium acetate precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Add 1/3 volume (4-5 mL) of 5 M Potassium Acetate and mix by inverting.
Incubate on ice (4°C) for 10 min without rotation.
Centrifuge at 5,000 rcf for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer supernatant to a new 15 mL Falcon tube and centrifuge again at 5,000 rcf for 10 min at 4°C.

steps.title: First Magnetic Bead Purification
steps.instruction: Bind and purify DNA using Sera-Mag beads.

substeps.instruction: Transfer supernatant to a new tube and add 1.2x binding buffer (ideally split across two 15 mL Falcon tubes).
Add 1 mL of 2% Sera-Mag beads (500 µL per Falcon tube if split).
Mix by inverting the tube 20 times and incubate with gentle agitation (rotator or shaker) for 1 h at room temperature.
Place the tube in a magnetic rack for 30 min or more until the solution becomes clear.
Remove the supernatant without disturbing the beads.
Wash the beads by filling the tube with 70% ethanol, letting beads settle, and pouring out the ethanol; repeat 2 more times or until clean.
Transfer beads into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube by dislodging them with 1 mL of ethanol per transfer.
Place the 2 mL Eppendorf tubes on the magnetic rack, remove supernatant, and consolidate all beads into one tube.
Remove all traces of ethanol and air dry the beads for 1-4 min (do not dry completely).
Using a wide-bore pipette tip, add 220 µL of nuclease-free water to the beads, gently resuspend, and incubate at room temperature for at least 10 min.
Transfer 200-220 µL of supernatant to a DNA LoBind eppendorf tube, avoiding bead carry-over.
Place the tube in the magnetic rack for ~30 min until the solution is clear.

steps.title: Gel Purification and Size Selection
steps.instruction: Purify and size-select DNA using an automated electrophoresis system.

substeps.instruction: Using a PippinHT (Sage Science) or similar system, gel purify approximately 30 µg of DNA following manufacturer's instructions (recommended 15 kb high pass, or 20 kb if DNA is plentiful).
Load 20 µL of DNA per lane (up to 3 µg per lane).
After separation, wait at least 45 min (up to overnight) to aid elution.
Collect the contents of all elution wells into a 1.5 mL DNA LoBind Eppendorf tube (approx. 300 µL).
Add 30 µL of 0.1% tween in electrophoresis buffer to each elution well, wait 5 min, and transfer the contents to the same 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube (total volume approx. 600 µL).

steps.title: Final DNA Recovery
steps.instruction: Perform a final bead cleanup to recover the purified DNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.2x binding buffer (approx. 720 µL) and 100 µL of 2% Sera-Mag beads to the 1.5 mL DNA LoBind Eppendorf tube; incubate for 5-10 min at room temperature.
Place on a magnetic rack for 5 min or until clear and discard the supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 1 mL of freshly prepared 70% ethanol while keeping the tube on the magnetic rack.
Remove all traces of ethanol and air dry the beads for 1-4 min.
Place on a magnetic rack for 5 min or until clear.
Elute with 60 µL of nuclease-free water, incubate for 10 min at room temperature, and transfer the eluted DNA to a new 1.5 mL DNA LoBind Eppendorf tube using a wide-bore pipette tip.

Optional: Perform a second elution by adding an additional 60 µL (or 100 µL as per alternative text) of nuclease-free water to the beads, resuspending, and transferring to a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Sequencing and Storage
steps.instruction: Prepare the library and store the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a library using Oxford Nanopore MinION (SQK-RAD004 or SQK-LSK109) following manufacturer's instructions, adjusting input DNA mass based on average length.
Load the MinION and perform sequencing, ensuring no air bubbles are introduced into the array.
Store DNA at 4°C to prevent freeze-thaw shearing.
